text:
Luke Evangelista cost the Devils a conditional 2028 first-round pick and a second when they got him from Nashville on Sept. 1, and the case for that price was last season: Evolving-Hockey had him sixth among 401 forwards in wins above replacement, driving play at both ends. Twenty-three games into his New Jersey career, the points have not followed. Twelve, with four on the power play, and none in his last four.

The process looks like the player they traded for. New Jersey takes 59% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, and his own chances are up to 1.06 expected goals per 60 minutes from 0.86 in Nashville. The problem is finishing, his and everyone's. The Devils have scored 6.7 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him out there, and his 1.84 points per 60 sits below the bottom of our talent range.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking pegged him as a setup man last season. That kind of player lives on teammates finishing. Watch whether his minutes, now drifting toward 15, hold while the luck turns.
